title: Cell cycle and cell division – mitosis and meiosis
blurb: What the cell cycle has to achieve; its phases (G1, S, G2, M; G0); the control system with three checkpoints (Start/G1-S, G2/M, metaphase-to-anaphase); Cdks and the four cyclin classes; APC/C triggering anaphase (securin → separase → cohesin).
h1: Cell cycle and cell division – mitosis and meiosis
lede: What the cell cycle has to achieve; its phases (G1, S, G2, M; G0); the control system with three checkpoints (Start/G1-S, G2/M, metaphase-to-anaphase); Cdks and the four cyclin classes; APC/C triggering anaphase (securin → separase → cohesin). The S phase: one replication per cycle through origin licensing, and cohesin holding sister chromatids. The five stages of mitosis (prophase, prometaphase, metaphase, anaphase A/B, telophase) and cytokinesis (contractile ring vs cell plate). Meiosis: two divisions; bivalents, tetrads, crossing-over and chiasmata; the five stages of prophase I (leptotene, zygotene, pachytene, diplotene, diakinesis); and how meiosis differs from mitosis.
six: Phases G1, S, G2, M, G0; the role of gap phases
Three checkpoints and what each checks
Cdk + cyclin; four cyclin types; APC/C controls metaphase→anaphase (not cyclin-dependent)
Licensing: DNA replicated only once per cycle
Five mitotic stages and what happens in each; anaphase A vs B

questions.q: The metaphase-to-anaphase transition is triggered by:
questions.e: It is not cyclin-dependent; APC/C(–Cdc20) triggers it. (Slides: s. 17)

questions.q: Which protein complex holds sister chromatids together until anaphase?
questions.e: Cohesin; separase cleaves it at anaphase. (Slides: s. 17, s. 20)

questions.q: In which phase does the nuclear envelope break down?

questions.answer: moving apart of the spindle poles
questions.e: A = kinetochore microtubules shorten; B = poles move apart. (Slides: s. 26)

questions.q: Which cyclins trigger entry into mitosis?
In plant cells, cytokinesis occurs by:
wrong: a contractile ring of actin and myosin
questions.e: Plants form a cell plate from fused vesicles. (Slides: s. 29)

questions.q: Which is the correct order of prophase I stages?
The synaptonemal complex is completed in:
In meiosis I the following separate:
questions.e: Meiosis I separates homologs; meiosis II separates sisters. (Slides: s. 30)

questions.q: A cell that leaves the cycle under unfavourable conditions in G1 enters:
What is checked at the G2/M checkpoint?
questions.answer: Completion of DNA replication and DNA integrity
questions.e: G2/M checks replication completion and DNA integrity. (Slides: s. 9)
Tetrad = the four chromatids of a bivalent. (Slides: s. 32)

cards.lede: Read the question, answer it out loud, then flip the card.

items.n: What is the basic function of the cell cycle?
items.a: To duplicate the DNA and segregate the copies into two genetically identical daughter cells.

items.n: Two major phases of the cell cycle?
items.a: S phase (DNA synthesis) and M phase (mitosis + cytokinesis).

items.n: Four phases of the eukaryotic cell cycle?
items.a: G1, S, G2, M.
A resting state entered from G1 under unfavourable conditions (temporary or permanent).

items.n: What happens in G1 if damage is severe?
items.a: Senescence or apoptosis.
Start (late G1/S), G2/M, metaphase-to-anaphase.
Completion of replication and integrity of DNA.
Correct kinetochore attachment and tension between sister chromatids.
Cyclin-dependent kinases: enzymes that phosphorylate target proteins and drive cell-cycle events.
Cyclins, which are made and degraded each cycle.
G1/S-cyclins, S-cyclins, M-cyclins, G1-cyclins.
Activate Cdks for entry into mitosis at G2/M; levels fall mid-mitosis.
APC/C (anaphase-promoting complex/cyclosome), not a cyclin.
APC/C–Cdc20 tags securin for degradation; freed separase cleaves cohesin; sisters separate.

items.n: How is DNA replicated only once per cycle?
items.a: Origin licensing: inactive helicase is loaded in G1, activated by S-Cdk in S, then removed so the origin can't fire again.
Cohesin, a ring of SMC proteins, from S phase until anaphase.
Prophase, prometaphase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase.
Chromosomes condense (condensin); the spindle assembles between the two centrosomes.
Nuclear envelope breaks down; chromosomes attach to the spindle via kinetochores.
A protein structure on the centromere linking the chromosome to spindle microtubules.
Chromosomes align at the spindle equator, with sisters attached to opposite poles.
A: kinetochore microtubules shorten. B: spindle poles move apart.
Aneuploidy.
Chromosomes decondense, nuclear envelopes re-form, the contractile ring starts dividing the cytoplasm.

items.n: Cytokinesis in animal vs plant cells?
items.a: Animals: contractile ring of actin + myosin II. Plants: cell plate from fused vesicles (pectins, then cellulose and hemicellulose).

items.n: What separates in meiosis I and in meiosis II?
items.a: I: homologous chromosomes. II: sister chromatids.
With programmed DNA double-strand breaks.
Bivalent = paired homologs; tetrad = their 4 chromatids; chiasma = visible crossover connection.

items.n: Five stages of prophase I in order?
items.a: Leptotene, zygotene, pachytene, diplotene, diakinesis.

items.n: In which stage is the synaptonemal complex complete?
items.a: Pachytene (homologs synapsed along their whole length).

items.n: In which stage do chiasmata become visible?
items.a: Diplotene (the synaptonemal complex disassembles).
Meiosis: 4 haploid cells. Mitosis: 2 diploid identical cells.
